title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of road illumination devices (lamps) and systems for power-driven vehicles (version 1.6.0)
scope_summary: R149 type-approves road illumination devices (lamps): driving-beam and passing-beam headlamps (asymmetrical and symmetrical), adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS), adaptive driving-beam (ADB), front fog lamps of Class F3 and cornering lamps of Class K. The vehicle categories depend on the device: L, M, N and T for asymmetrical headlamps; M, N and L3 for AFS; L3 for ADB; L and T for symmetrical headlamps; L3, L4, L5, L7, M, N and T for front fog lamps; and M, N and T for cornering lamps.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to the following road illumination devices (lamps): Headlamps emitting a driving-beam and/or an asymmetrical passing-beam for vehicles of categories L, M, N and T Adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS) for vehicles of categories M, N and L3 Adaptive Driving-Beam (ADB) for vehicles of category L3 Headlamps emitting a driving-beam and/or a symmetrical passing-beam for vehicles of categories L and T Front fog lamps for vehicles of categories L3, L4, L5, L7, M, N and T Cornering lamps for vehicles of categories M, N and T.
applies_to_components: Headlamps emitting a driving-beam and/or an asymmetrical passing-beam (Classes A, B, C, V, RA)
Headlamps emitting a driving-beam and/or a symmetrical passing-beam (Classes AS, BS, CS, DS)
Adaptive front-lighting systems (AFS) and their installation units / lighting units
Adaptive driving-beam (ADB), incl. ADB for category L3
Front fog lamps of Class F3 (white or selective yellow)
Light source modules used in road illumination devices (Annex 9)
Electronic light source control gear forming part of the lamp
Additional lighting units for bend lighting on headlamps for L and T vehicles
Plastic outer lenses and plastic light-transmitting components of road illumination devices (Annex 8)
Mechanical/electromechanical beam-switching and bend-lighting devices incorporated in headlamps/AFS
relation_to_other_regulations: Combines the provisions of UN Regulations Nos. 19 (front fog lamps), 98 (gas-discharge headlamps), 112 (asymmetrical headlamps), 113 (symmetrical headlamps), 119 (cornering lamps) and 123 (AFS) into a single regulation.
Definitions of UN R48 apply unless otherwise specified here or in the installation Regulations Nos. 53, 74 and 86.
Sections 5 and 6 of installation Regulations R48, R53, R74 and R86 apply where they can be verified at lamp approval.
Replaceable light sources must be approved to UN R37, R99 and/or R128; LED substitute light sources fall under R128.
An AFS (or an ADB/AFS for L3) approved separately from the vehicle type under R48/R53 must also be approved to UN R10 (EMC).
Refers to R48 para 6.22 and R53 paras 6.16/6.18 for AFS/ADB installation, and to R48 for Driver Assistance Projection and rearward white-light visibility.
Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may each be approved to this or another Regulation.
Refers to R.E.5 (standard light sources), R.E.3, IEC 60061 (holders) and IEC 60809 (non-replaceable filament light sources).

defined_terms.term: Road illumination devices (lamps) of different types
defined_terms.label: type
defined_terms.definition: Road illumination devices that differ in essentials such as trade name or mark, optical system characteristics, optical-altering components, traffic side suitability, kind of beam, AFS functions, or light source category / light source module code.

defined_terms.label: main mode
defined_terms.definition: For a headlamp, the principal passing-beam if present, otherwise the front fog lamp, otherwise the driving-beam; for an AFS, the passing-beam mode drawing the highest total wattage.

defined_terms.label: headlamp
defined_terms.definition: A road illumination device emitting a driving-beam and/or a passing-beam (asymmetrical or symmetrical) (definition per UN R48).

defined_terms.label: AFS
defined_terms.definition: A system providing front-lighting functions (passing-beam classes C, E, V, W and driving-beam R) with modes adapted to conditions, built from installation units and lighting units (per UN R48).

defined_terms.label: ADB
defined_terms.definition: A driving-beam that adapts gradually according to a sensor system, approved here incl. for category L3 vehicles (per UN R48/R53).

defined_terms.label: front fog lamp
defined_terms.definition: A lamp improving road illumination in fog, approved as Class F3, emitting white or selective yellow light.

defined_terms.label: cornering lamp
defined_terms.definition: A lamp of Class K providing supplementary illumination of the road area to the side the vehicle is about to turn.

defined_terms.label: matched pair
defined_terms.definition: Left and right lamps operating together as a pair, allowed for passing-beams C, V, AS, BS, CS, DS, driving-beams A, B, BS, CS, DS, ADB and front fog lamps (symbol prefix 'Y').

defined_terms.label: light source module
defined_terms.definition: A replaceable or non-replaceable optical module containing light source(s), identified by a specific code starting with 'MD'.

defined_terms.label: ALU
defined_terms.definition: A lighting unit used with an L or T category headlamp to produce bend lighting, marked with a code starting with 'ALU'.

defined_terms.label: control gear
defined_terms.definition: Electronic device operating a light source or light source module; when outside the lamp body it is marked with its identification code and rated voltage.

defined_terms.label: LED substitute
defined_terms.definition: An LED light source approved under UN R128 to replace a filament light source category; its use does not change the lamp type, but photometric tests must be repeated with it.

defined_terms.label: principal passing-beam
defined_terms.definition: The passing-beam produced without contribution from bend-lighting additional sources, used for the minimum and maximum luminous flux requirements (Tables 3a/3b/4).

applicability_hints: Any LED headlamp, AFS or fog/cornering lamp module with a non-replaceable LED light source module falls under R149 and Annex 9; replaceable modules need an 'MD' code and tamperproof design.
An electronic driver/ballast (light source control gear) outside the lamp body is part of the lamp approval and must carry an ID code and rated voltage.
Standalone AFS/ADB approval not tied to a vehicle approval additionally requires R10 EMC approval.
Former R19, R98, R112, R113, R119 and R123 products (fog lamps, HID headlamps, symmetrical motorcycle headlamps, cornering lamps, AFS) are now approved under R149.
ADB/adaptive main-beam for M/N vehicles is approved as part of an AFS (AFS-R); ADB for L3 is a separate class.
Plastic outer lenses (except cornering lamps and Class AS) require material samples and Annex 8 tests; plastic inner parts of fog lamps need UV testing unless low-UV sources are used.
Additional lighting units providing bend lighting on L/T headlamps must be marked with an 'ALU' code.
Lamps approved for use with R128 LED substitute light sources require repeated photometry with those sources.
Grouped or combined assemblies (e.g. headlamp with DRL/position lamp) need each function approved to R149 or another applicable Regulation, e.g. R148.
Headlamps with Driver Assistance Projection must declare the projection zone.
Replacement lamps using restricted light source categories are limited to vehicles in use originally fitted with them.
Beam-switching or bend-lighting actuators (mechanical/electromechanical) inside headlamps fall under the 4.11 durability and failure requirements.
